summary: Backend-only validation completed for new POST /api/support/contact trusted ingestion flow, plus site-menus contact gate and payment/google regressions. All targeted tests passed after strengthening unauthorized-persistence and bell-readability assertions.
action_items: No blocking fixes required in requested scope.
Optional hardening: reject unknown support-contact payload keys explicitly (currently ignored by model parsing).
critical_code_review_comments: POST /api/support/contact enforces X-PCStore-Secret with compare_digest and returns 401 on missing/wrong secret before any insert.
Trusted contact persistence and bell notification shape match required fields: support_messages status=unread and notifications type=support_message/read=false with customer+subject context.
Admin email recipient and subject are server-selected via SUPPORT_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL and EMAIL_FROM_NAME; request payload cannot override recipient, HTML, or provider key in endpoint logic.
Email HTML escapes customer name/email/subject/message before managed send call.
seed_data_creation: Temporary support_messages and notifications test records were created and cleaned up within test teardown; no retained test records from this run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: I first ran a broader suite including test_notifications_scope and observed one non-scope brittle assertion due /api/notifications default limit pagination affecting type-count checks; then executed focused scope suite (support/site-menus/payment/google) with all green. Use notification queries with explicit high limit or DB-backed assertions for stable count-delta checks.
rca of the issue: No product defect reproduced in scope. One transient regression-file failure in broader run came from test methodology: counting notification types from the default capped list can hide +1 deltas when older rows roll off page.
